notes_for_editor: Story is moderate: the 1898-1902 construction is well documented (NRHP + Light-House Board reports 1897-1901; 1902 report not in corpus). Keeper stories are thin: roster is from USLHS only, no logs found; Chronicling America searches (up to 1935) gave only a 1905 Evening Capital note of an assistant 'Henry [surname lost to OCR]' transferred to Thomas Point and a 1918 notice of a boy drowned between Point No Point and the light; neither used. The 1926 Bulletin item (PDF p.31) says 'July 5' within the 1926 volume; year inferred as 1926 and consistent with Simpson's roster dates. The 1926 radio-set letters are from three keepers (Hooper Island, Ragged Point, Thimble Shoal); Lighthouse Friends attributes one quoted letter to Hooper Island but the Bulletin OCR does not make clear which, so no quote is attributed. Disputes: 1936 vs 1937 electrification, lens maker spelling Babier/Barbier. Ownership: USLHS archive and Lighthouse Centers list Cucé/The Lighthouse Centers as owner; the exact legal owner (individual vs. nonprofit) was not verified. Patch says the GSA 'transferred ownership to the USLHS in 2006'; LF says offered 2006 and deed May 2009. NRHP's 'only caisson light with watch room' claim is cited to the nomination. Fiscal-year reports: 1899 report covers to June 1899; 1900 report covers 1899-1900. LHB scan pages cited rather than printed pages (index suggests 1899 p.102, 1900 p.97).
